s201.content:
Campion was a brilliant Oxford scholar admired by Queen Elizabeth I. Troubled in conscience, he left England, was reconciled to the Catholic Church, and became a Jesuit priest.

He returned secretly in 1580 to minister to persecuted Catholics, and his open letter "Campion’s Brag" challenged the government to debate. Betrayed and captured, he was tortured on the rack and hanged, drawn, and quartered at Tyburn. He is one of the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales.
s201.intercession: St. Edmund Campion, pray for us. Give us the courage to bear witness to the truth with charity and joy. Amen.

s202.content:
Margaret was the wife of a butcher in York and mother of three. She converted to Catholicism when it was illegal and hid priests in a secret room in her house so that Mass could be celebrated.

Arrested in 1586, she refused to plead so that her children and servants would not be forced to testify. She was pressed to death under a heavy door loaded with stones. She is called "the Pearl of York."
s202.intercession: St. Margaret Clitherow, pray for us. Strengthen mothers and families who suffer for their faith, and help us to treasure the Mass. Amen.

s203.content:
Peter was a Dutch Jesuit who did more than anyone to restore the Catholic faith in Germany and Central Europe after the Reformation. He preached tirelessly, founded colleges, and attended the Council of Trent.

His catechisms, written in clear question-and-answer form, went through hundreds of editions and taught the faith to generations. He is called the "Second Apostle of Germany" and was named a Doctor of the Church in 1925.
s203.intercession: St. Peter Canisius, pray for us. Bless all who teach the faith, and help us to know our faith well and to explain it with patience. Amen.

s204.content:
Turibius was a Spanish lawyer and judge appointed archbishop of Lima while still a layman. He traveled thousands of miles across the Andes on foot and by mule, visiting remote villages, learning the native languages, and confirming perhaps half a million people, including St. Rose of Lima.

He defended the indigenous peoples against abuse by Spanish officials, founded the first seminary in the Americas, and held councils to reform the Church in Peru.
s204.intercession: St. Turibius, pray for us. Bless bishops with a shepherd’s heart, and help us to defend the dignity of every people. Amen.

s205.content:
Louise was a Parisian widow and mother who, after years of anxiety and spiritual struggle, found her calling under the guidance of St. Vincent de Paul. Together they founded the Daughters of Charity in 1633.

Unlike enclosed nuns, the Daughters went into the streets, homes, and hospitals to serve the sick, orphans, and prisoners. Louise trained them with great practical wisdom. She is a patron of social workers.
s205.intercession: St. Louise de Marillac, pray for us. Help us to see Christ in the poor and to serve them with competence and tenderness. Amen.

s206.content:
Pedro was a teenage catechist from the Visayas in the Philippines who traveled with Spanish Jesuit missionaries to the Mariana Islands. There he taught the faith and assisted Fr. Diego Luis de San Vitores, now Blessed.

In 1672, when they baptized an infant against the father’s wishes, a mob attacked them. Pedro could have escaped but stayed to defend the priest, and both were killed. He was canonized in 2012.
s206.intercession: St. Pedro Calungsod, young catechist and martyr, pray for us. Inspire young people to share their faith and to stand by those who serve the Church. Amen.

s207.content:
John was a wealthy canon of Reims who became involved, almost by accident, in opening free schools for poor boys. He gave away his fortune, lived with the teachers he trained, and founded the Brothers of the Christian Schools.

He pioneered teaching in the students’ own language rather than Latin, grouping children into classes, and training teachers in colleges. Pope Pius XII named him patron of all teachers.
s207.intercession: St. John Baptist de La Salle, pray for us. Bless all teachers with patience and love, and help every child to be well taught. Amen.

s208.content:
Paolo Danei was an Italian merchant’s son who, after a vision, became convinced that the Passion of Christ is the greatest proof of God’s love. He founded the Congregation of the Passion, the Passionists, to preach the crucified Christ.

He was a renowned missionary preacher and spiritual director, though he himself endured decades of spiritual darkness. His letters remain treasured guides to prayer.
s208.intercession: St. Paul of the Cross, pray for us. Help us to see in Christ’s Passion the depth of God’s love, and to bear our own crosses with faith. Amen.

s209.content:
Philippine was a French Religious of the Sacred Heart who dreamed for years of serving the Native Americans. At forty-nine she sailed to America and opened the first free school west of the Mississippi, near St. Louis.

At seventy-one she finally went to live among the Potawatomi in Kansas. Unable to learn their language, she prayed for hours each day, and they called her "Woman Who Prays Always." She was canonized in 1988.
s209.intercession: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne, pray for us. Teach us perseverance in our callings and faithfulness in prayer. Amen.

s210.content:
Anne-Thérèse Guérin was a French Sister of Providence sent in 1840 to the wilderness of Indiana. With five companions she founded the Sisters of Providence of Saint Mary-of-the-Woods and opened schools, orphanages, and pharmacies.

She faced fires, crop failures, illness, and conflict with her bishop, always trusting in Providence. "Put yourself gently into the hands of Providence," she wrote. She was canonized in 2006.
s210.intercession: St. Théodore Guérin, pray for us. Help us to trust in God’s Providence through every hardship. Amen.

s211.content:
Peter was a French Marist priest who volunteered for the missions of the South Pacific. He landed on the island of Futuna in 1837, where he learned the language, cared for the sick, and slowly won the people’s trust.

When the king’s son asked to be baptized, the king ordered Peter killed, and he was clubbed to death. Within a few years almost the entire island had become Catholic. He is the first martyr of Oceania.
s211.intercession: St. Peter Chanel, pray for us. Bless missionaries in distant lands, and help us to sow the Gospel with patience and love. Amen.

s212.content:
Dominic was a peasant boy who entered St. John Bosco’s school in Turin at twelve. On the day of his First Communion he wrote: "Death rather than sin." Don Bosco saw in him a soul of rare goodness.

He was known for his cheerfulness, his kindness to other boys, and his skill at making peace. He founded the Company of the Immaculate Conception to help classmates. He died at fourteen and is the patron of choirboys and young people.
s212.intercession: St. Dominic Savio, pray for us. Help young people to choose goodness with joy, and to be peacemakers among their friends. Amen.

s213.content:
Francesco Possenti was a popular, fashionable young man in Spoleto who loved dancing and the theater. During a procession with an image of Our Lady, he felt her call him personally and soon entered the Passionists.

There he took the name Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows and became known for his joy and his devotion to Mary’s sorrows. He died of tuberculosis at twenty-three, before ordination. He is a patron of students and youth.
s213.intercession: St. Gabriel, pray for us. Help young people to leave behind every vanity and to give their hearts wholly to Christ through Mary. Amen.

s214.content:
Anthony was a Catalan weaver who became a priest and a tireless missionary preacher. He founded the Claretian Missionaries and, as archbishop of Santiago de Cuba, survived an assassination attempt while working to end slavery and corruption.

Later he served as confessor to Queen Isabella II of Spain. He founded a religious publishing house and wrote over a hundred books and pamphlets. He is a patron of weavers and Catholic publishers.
s214.intercession: St. Anthony Mary Claret, pray for us. Bless all who spread the Gospel through the written word, and make us zealous for souls. Amen.

s215.content:
Daniel was an Italian priest who devoted his life to Central Africa. His motto was "Save Africa with Africa," and he insisted on training African priests and catechists at a time when few Europeans believed in their abilities.

He founded missionary institutes for men and women, fought the slave trade, and became the first Catholic bishop of Central Africa. He died in Khartoum at fifty and was canonized in 2003.
s215.intercession: St. Daniel Comboni, pray for us. Bless the Church in Africa, and help us to respect and draw out the gifts of every people. Amen.

s216.content:
Mariam was born in Galilee to a poor Melkite Greek Catholic family and orphaned at three. As a young servant she refused to convert to Islam and was attacked and left for dead, an ordeal she believed Our Lady helped her survive.

As a Carmelite nun called Mary of Jesus Crucified, she experienced ecstasies and the stigmata, and helped found Carmels in India and Bethlehem. Her prayer to the Holy Spirit is still widely loved.
s216.intercession: St. Mariam of Jesus Crucified, pray for us. Ask the Holy Spirit to enlighten us, and bring peace to the Holy Land. Amen.

s217.content:
Joseph was a priest from the Dolomites who joined the Society of the Divine Word and in 1879 was sent to southern Shandong in China. He adopted Chinese dress and customs and resolved to become "Chinese among the Chinese."

He trained Chinese catechists and priests and endured beatings and hardship. He died of typhus caught while nursing the sick. "The language of love," he said, "is the only language every person understands."
s217.intercession: St. Joseph Freinademetz, pray for us. Help us to speak the language of love that every person understands. Amen.

s218.content:
Élisabeth Catez was a lively, strong-willed girl from Dijon and a gifted pianist. She entered the Carmel there at twenty-one and discovered her calling to be a "praise of glory" to the Holy Trinity dwelling within her soul.

She died of Addison’s disease at twenty-six. Her letters and her prayer "O my God, Trinity whom I adore" have helped countless people discover God’s presence within. She was canonized in 2016.
s218.intercession: St. Elizabeth of the Trinity, pray for us. Help us to find the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit dwelling in our hearts. Amen.

s219.content:
Charles was a wealthy French cavalry officer and explorer who lost his faith in youth. Moved by the prayer of Muslims in Morocco, he began searching for God and returned to the Church in 1886.

He became a priest and lived as a hermit among the Tuareg people of the Sahara, seeking to be a "universal brother" through friendship, hospitality, and adoration of the Eucharist. He was killed by raiders in 1916 and canonized in 2022.
s219.intercession: St. Charles de Foucauld, pray for us. Teach us to abandon ourselves to the Father and to be brothers and sisters to all. Amen.

s220.content:
Juana Fernández Solar was a cheerful, athletic Chilean girl who loved horseback riding and swimming. From an early age she felt drawn to the Carmelites and wrote letters and a diary full of love for Christ.

She entered the Carmel of Los Andes at nineteen and died of typhus less than a year later. Her joyful spirituality made her the first saint of Chile, canonized in 1993.
s220.intercession: St. Teresa of the Andes, pray for us. Help young people to find their joy in loving Jesus. Amen.

s221.content:
José was a Mexican boy who joined the Cristero rebellion at thirteen, during the government’s persecution of the Church, serving as a flag bearer. Captured by federal troops, he was told he could go free if he renounced his faith.

He refused. Soldiers cut the soles of his feet and forced him to walk to the cemetery, where he was killed. At each step he cried "¡Viva Cristo Rey!" He was canonized in 2016.
s221.intercession: St. José, pray for us. Give children and young people the courage to proclaim that Christ is King. Amen.

s222.content:
Leopold was a Croatian Capuchin friar, barely four and a half feet tall, with a speech impediment and poor health. He longed to work for the reunion of the Eastern Orthodox with the Catholic Church.

Instead his superiors kept him in Padua, where he spent over thirty years hearing confessions for up to fifteen hours a day, known for his gentleness and mercy. He was canonized in 1983 and is a patron of confessors.
s222.intercession: St. Leopold, pray for us. Bless all confessors, and help us to come to the sacrament of mercy with trust. Amen.

s223.content:
Titus was a Dutch Carmelite priest, professor of philosophy, and journalist. When the Nazis occupied the Netherlands, he carried a letter from the bishops to Catholic newspapers instructing them to refuse Nazi propaganda.

Arrested and sent to Dachau, he comforted fellow prisoners and prayed for his guards. He was killed by lethal injection in 1942, after giving his rosary to the nurse who administered it. He was canonized in 2022.
s223.intercession: St. Titus Brandsma, pray for us. Give journalists courage to tell the truth, and help us to love even those who persecute us. Amen.

s224.content:
Maria Rita Lopes Pontes was a Brazilian Franciscan sister in Salvador, Bahia, who began by sheltering sick people in abandoned houses and then in a chicken coop beside her convent. That coop grew into one of the largest hospitals in Brazil.

Sister Dulce slept sitting in a chair for decades as penance, and was called "the Good Angel of Bahia." She was canonized in 2019 as the first Brazilian-born woman saint.
s224.intercession: St. Dulce, pray for us. Open our eyes to the poor and the sick around us, and help us to begin serving them today. Amen.

s225.content:
These 120 martyrs of China include priests, catechists, laypeople, and children, killed for the faith between 1648 and 1930, many during the Boxer Rebellion of 1900.

Augustine Zhao Rong was a soldier who escorted a condemned bishop to his execution, was moved by his witness, and became a priest himself. He died in prison in 1815. The martyrs were canonized together by Pope St. John Paul II in 2000.
s225.intercession: Holy martyrs of China, pray for us. Strengthen the Church in China and all Christians who suffer for their faith. Amen.

s226.content:
These 117 martyrs of Vietnam include bishops, priests, catechists, and laypeople, killed during waves of persecution in the 18th and 19th centuries. Many were tortured and beheaded; some were strangled or burned.

Andrew Dũng-Lạc was a Vietnamese parish priest who was arrested several times and once ransomed by his parishioners before his execution in 1839. The martyrs were canonized together in 1988.
s226.intercession: Holy martyrs of Vietnam, pray for us. Give us courage to bear witness to Christ, and bless the Church in Vietnam. Amen.

s227.content:
Simeon was a Syrian shepherd boy whose hunger for prayer drove him to ever more severe forms of solitude. When crowds of pilgrims would not leave him in peace, he climbed onto a pillar near Aleppo.

He lived on top of pillars for over thirty-five years, praying, fasting, and preaching to the crowds below, and settling disputes among them. The ruins of the great church built around his pillar still stand in Syria.
s227.intercession: St. Simeon, pray for us. Help us to lift our hearts above the noise of the world and to persevere in prayer. Amen.

s228.content:
Marguerite was a Canadian widow whose husband, a bootlegger, left her with debts and two surviving sons. She supported her family with a small shop while caring for the poor of Montreal.

In 1737 she and three companions founded the Sisters of Charity, known as the Grey Nuns, and later took over the city’s failing General Hospital. She was the first saint born in Canada, canonized in 1990.
s228.intercession: St. Marguerite d’Youville, pray for us. Comfort those in difficult marriages and widowhood, and teach us to welcome the poor. Amen.

s229.content:
Marie Guyart was a widow from Tours who ran her brother-in-law’s shipping business before entering the Ursulines, leaving her twelve-year-old son in the care of family. In 1639 she sailed to New France.

In Quebec she founded the first school for girls in North America, learned the Algonquin and Huron languages, and wrote dictionaries and catechisms in them. Her letters are a treasure of mystical and historical writing.
s229.intercession: St. Marie of the Incarnation, pray for us. Bless mothers, teachers, and missionaries, and help us to find God in the midst of busy lives. Amen.

s230.content:
Jeanne was a French domestic servant who one winter night in 1839 carried a blind, paralyzed old woman home and gave her own bed. More elderly poor followed, and the Little Sisters of the Poor were born.

Jeanne begged door to door for her old people. Later, pushed aside from leadership, she spent her last twenty-seven years in humble obscurity, teaching the novices. Her sisters now serve the elderly worldwide.
s230.intercession: St. Jeanne Jugan, pray for us. Help us to honor and care for the elderly, and to accept humbly whatever God asks. Amen.

s231.content:
Rafqa (Rebecca) was a Maronite nun from Lebanon. In 1885 she asked God to let her share in the sufferings of Christ, and soon began to lose her sight to an agonizing illness.

She spent her remaining twenty-nine years in pain, eventually blind and paralyzed, yet always grateful and at peace, weaving and praying in the convent of St. Joseph in Jrabta. She was canonized in 2001.
s231.intercession: St. Rafqa, pray for us. Help the sick to unite their sufferings with Christ, and give them patience and peace. Amen.

s232.content:
Joseph was a priest from Goa in India who learned that Catholics in Sri Lanka had been left without priests under persecution by the Dutch. He traveled there disguised as a beggar and ministered secretly for more than twenty years.

He translated prayers into Tamil and Sinhala, cared for smallpox victims when no one else would, and rebuilt the Church on the island. He is called the "Apostle of Sri Lanka" and was canonized in 2015.
s232.intercession: St. Joseph Vaz, pray for us. Bless the Church in Sri Lanka and India, and help us to serve Christ in the forgotten. Amen.

s233.content:
Titus was a Greek convert and one of St. Paul’s most trusted companions. Paul brought him to the Council of Jerusalem as an example of a Gentile Christian who had not been circumcised, and later sent him to settle troubles in Corinth.

Paul left him to organize the Church on the island of Crete, and wrote him the Letter to Titus with instructions for appointing elders. Tradition says he died there as bishop in old age.
s233.intercession: St. Titus, pray for us. Bless all who are entrusted with building up the Church, and help us to live soberly, justly, and devoutly. Amen.

s234.content:
Joseph was a wealthy member of the Jewish council who had become a secret disciple of Jesus. After the Crucifixion he went boldly to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.

With Nicodemus he wrapped the body in linen with spices and laid it in his own new tomb, cut in the rock. Medieval legends connected him with the Holy Grail and with Glastonbury in England.
s234.intercession: St. Joseph of Arimathea, pray for us. Give us the courage to show our love for Christ openly, and bless all who care for the dead. Amen.

s235.content:
Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, was a close friend of Jesus. When he died, Jesus wept at his tomb, then called him out alive after four days, a sign that pointed to Jesus’ own Resurrection.

Many came to believe because of him, and the chief priests plotted to kill him too. Since 2021, the Church celebrates Martha, Mary, and Lazarus together as friends of the Lord.
s235.intercession: St. Lazarus, raised by the voice of Christ, pray for us. Call us out of every darkness into new life, and help us to be true friends of Jesus. Amen.

s236.content:
Dismas is the name tradition gives to the "good thief" crucified beside Jesus. While the other criminal mocked, he admitted his own guilt, defended Jesus’ innocence, and asked to be remembered when Jesus came into his kingdom.

Jesus promised him paradise that very day. He is the only person in the Gospels assured of salvation by Jesus himself, and a sign that it is never too late to turn to God.
s236.intercession: St. Dismas, pray for us. Help all prisoners and all who have done great wrong to turn to Jesus with trust, as you did. Amen.

s237.content:
According to tradition, Veronica was a woman of Jerusalem who, moved with pity as Jesus carried his cross, stepped forward to wipe his face with her veil. The image of his face remained on the cloth.

Her act of courage and compassion is remembered in the Sixth Station of the Cross. Her name is often explained as "true image."
s237.intercession: St. Veronica, pray for us. Give us the courage to offer small acts of mercy to those who suffer, and let the face of Christ be imprinted on our hearts. Amen.

s238.content:
Elizabeth, a relative of Mary, and her husband Zechariah were righteous before God but childless into old age. The angel Gabriel announced that she would bear a son, John the Baptist.

When Mary visited her, the baby leapt in her womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, greeted Mary as the mother of her Lord. Her words form part of the Hail Mary.
s238.intercession: St. Elizabeth, pray for us. Comfort those who long for children, and help us to recognize Christ and welcome Him with joy. Amen.

s239.content:
Priscilla and her husband Aquila were Jewish Christians and tentmakers who were expelled from Rome by the Emperor Claudius. In Corinth they took St. Paul into their home and worked alongside him.

They later taught the gifted preacher Apollos the way of God more accurately, and hosted a church in their house. Paul called them his fellow workers who had risked their necks for him.
s239.intercession: Sts. Priscilla and Aquila, pray for us. Bless married couples who serve the Church together, and make our homes places of welcome. Amen.

s240.content:
According to the historian Eusebius, Fabian was a layman who came to Rome for a papal election when a dove landed on his head, and the people took it as a sign and chose him.

He organized the Church of Rome into districts, cared for the catacombs, and sent missionaries to Gaul. He was one of the first victims of the Emperor Decius’ persecution. He shares his feast with St. Sebastian.
s240.intercession: Pope St. Fabian, pray for us. Help us to accept God’s call even when it surprises us, and to serve faithfully to the end. Amen.
